column4: The exact same gothic cathedral seen in reverse, from the stage looking down the long central aisle toward tall closed double doors at the far end; deep perspective of large graphic pillars, rows of pews, chandeliers and banners matching the reference interior.

One tall gothic leaded stained-glass window filling the frame, showing a serene icon of the same girl from the character sheet (long orange hair, flower ornament on her right side of the picture), arms low and open, palms up, gentle downcast gaze; strong lead lines divide the glass into large readable pieces; the flower is not a halo.

Inside the same cathedral, rows of faceless worshippers in coal-black hoods sit in wooden pews, heads bowed over closed blank ledgers on their laps; three clearly separated depth rows, candles and pillars between them, seen from slightly above and behind.

A stout clothbound rulebook with an orange cover and coal-black gothic embossing rests closed on a carved gothic wooden lectern, cathedral pillars and candles behind; spine and page edge clearly visible.
Overhead view of a ledger lying open on a carved wooden pew rail, a blank ruled two-page spread with wide margins, a ribbon bookmark, the edge of a hymn book and a candle stub beside it.

A side wing of the cathedral with a receding row of tall narrow dressing mirrors in heavy carved coal frames; the tallest center mirror has a clear blank ivory reflective surface; draped fabric, a hat stand and a small stool add life.

Three tall side stained-glass windows in a cathedral wall depicting the same orange-haired girl: kneeling in prayer, serving with a tray, standing with a halo; repeated silhouettes link them; a blank nameplate under each window.
A cathedral wall holding a grid of small identical ornate puppet-theater prosceniums arranged like a bank of screens, each with tiny curtains pulled open and an empty interior; distinct frame edges.

Long shadowed shelves holding rows of identical retired porcelain doll heads of the same orange-haired maid model, eyes closed, each with a small blank hanging tag on a string; dust and cobweb shapes; room for a slow sideways pan.
The same cathedral stage, now with a large square floor hatch thrown open in the wooden boards, revealing a dark drop lined with bookshelves below; camera matches the reference stage view.

A steep vertical shaft descending deep underground, its walls lined with stacked books and repeating shelf ledges, a ladder and dangling lamps; the middle route open for a falling figure; top and bottom bands simple enough to crop.
Tall gothic double cathedral doors seen from inside the dark nave, closed, with a readable center seam, heavy iron hinges, strong carved jambs and threshold, pews in the foreground.

An isolated sprite sheet on a plain ivory background: separated porcelain chips and shards, leaded stained-glass shards, one brass-style winding key shown at several rotations, a few flower petals; each shape separated by a wide empty gutter.
